ujjain.s: Ujjain is an ancient city in central India on the Shipra River, one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism. It was a major commercial and administrative centre on routes linking northern India with the western coast.

ukiyo-e.s: Ukiyo-e, meaning 'pictures of the floating world', is a genre of Japanese woodblock prints and paintings that flourished from the seventeenth to the nineteenth centuries. It depicted actors, courtesans, landscapes and scenes of urban life.

ukraine.s: Ukraine is a country in eastern Europe whose fertile steppe lands have been contested by many powers. Much of it formed part of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, where the Khmelnytsky uprising of 1648 began the loss of eastern territories to Russia.

ulama.s: The ulama are the community of Muslim religious scholars, trained in Islamic law, theology and scripture. They staffed courts, schools and mosques and often mediated between rulers and subjects.

ulpian.s: Ulpian was a Roman jurist of the early third century CE and one of the most influential legal writers in Roman history. He served as praetorian prefect under Severus Alexander and was killed by the Praetorian Guard.

ulugh-beg.s: Ulugh Beg was a Timurid ruler and astronomer, a grandson of Timur, who governed Samarkand for decades and died in 1449. He built a great observatory and madrasa in Samarkand and sponsored astronomical tables of remarkable accuracy.

ulugh-beg-observatory.s: The Ulugh Beg Observatory was an astronomical observatory built in Samarkand in the 1420s by the Timurid ruler Ulugh Beg. Its huge meridian arc allowed precise measurements, and the astronomers who worked there produced a star catalogue and astronomical tables.

umar-din.s: Umar Din was a sultan of the Walashma dynasty in the Adal Sultanate in the sixteenth century. Accounts of the Adal Sultanate note that Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi held real power as leader of the jihad against Christian Ethiopia while maintaining a nominal Walashma sultan,…

umar-ibn-al-khattab.s: Umar ibn al-Khattab was the second caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 634 to 644 CE. Under his leadership Muslim armies conquered Syria, Iraq, Egypt and much of Iran, and he established key institutions such as the diwan for paying soldiers and garrison cities.

umayyad-caliphate.s: The Umayyad Caliphate was the second Islamic caliphate, ruled by the Umayyad family from Damascus from 661 to 750 CE. It expanded Muslim rule from Iberia and North Africa to Central Asia and the Indus valley, and established Arabic as the language of administration.

umayyad-conquest-of-hispania.s: The Umayyad conquest of Hispania was the Muslim conquest of most of the Iberian Peninsula beginning in 711 CE. Forces led by Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from North Africa and defeated the Visigothic king Roderic, and within a few years most of the peninsula was under Umayyad control.

umayyad-conquest-of-sind.s: The Umayyad conquest of Sind was the campaign of 711 CE in which forces led by Muhammad ibn Qasim conquered Sind, in the lower Indus valley in present-day Pakistan. It brought the region under the Umayyad Caliphate and marked the eastern limit of early Arab expansion into…

unequal-treaties.s: Unequal treaties is a term for agreements imposed on East Asian states by Western powers in the nineteenth century, granting privileges such as extraterritoriality, fixed tariffs and treaty ports. China and Japan were both subject to them.

unesco-world-heritage-site.s: A UNESCO World Heritage Site is a place recognised by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization as having outstanding cultural or natural value. The Chogha Zanbil ziggurat built under Untash-Napirisha holds this status.

union-of-krewo.s: The Union of Krewo was an agreement of 1385 under which Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agreed to accept Catholic Christianity and marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland, becoming King of Poland. It created a personal union between Poland and Lithuania.

union-of-lublin.s: The Union of Lublin was the agreement of 1569 that transformed the personal union of Poland and Lithuania into a single state, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The two parts retained separate administrations and armies but shared an elected monarch and a common Sejm.

united-nations.s: The United Nations is an international organisation founded in 1945 to maintain peace and promote cooperation among states, with its headquarters in New York. A reproduction of the Egyptian–Hittite peace treaty of Kadesh hangs at the United Nations headquarters.

united-states.s: The United States is a federal republic in North America that became independent from Britain in 1776 and grew into a major world power. It defeated the Spanish Empire in 1898, acquiring Spain's remaining overseas colonies, and was the principal adversary of the Empire of…

universal-suffrage.s: Universal suffrage is the right of all adult citizens to vote, regardless of property, class or, in its full form, sex. The German Empire introduced universal male suffrage for elections to the Reichstag in 1871.

untash-napirisha.s: Untash-Napirisha was a king of Elam in the fourteenth century BCE. He built the religious complex of Chogha Zanbil near Susa, centred on a great ziggurat.

uparika.s: An uparika was a provincial governor in the Gupta Empire. The empire was divided into provinces called bhuktis, each administered by an uparika, frequently a member of the royal family.

upemba-depression.s: The Upemba Depression is a low-lying basin of lakes, marshes and fertile land along the upper Lualaba River in the south-east of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo. Archaeological sites there show long continuous occupation.

upper-egypt.s: Upper Egypt is the southern part of Egypt, the narrow Nile Valley stretching from around Memphis southwards to the First Cataract at Aswan. It was home to Thebes, the religious centre of the New Kingdom.

upper-mesopotamia.s: Upper Mesopotamia is the northern part of the land between the Tigris and Euphrates, covering parts of present-day northern Iraq, north-eastern Syria and south-eastern Turkey. Rain-fed agriculture and trade routes supported cities such as Assur and Nineveh, making it the…

ur.s: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in southern Mesopotamia, near the former course of the Euphrates in present-day Iraq. It reached its height as the capital of the Third Dynasty of Ur, or Neo-Sumerian Empire, under Ur-Nammu and his successors, who built its great ziggurat.

ural-mountains.s: The Ural Mountains are a north–south mountain range in Russia, traditionally regarded as the boundary between Europe and Asia. Under Ivan IV Russian expansion crossed the Urals into Siberia, a process accelerated by Yermak Timofeyevich's Cossack campaigns from 1581 onward.

urdu.s: Urdu is an Indo-Aryan language closely related to Hindi, written in a Perso-Arabic script and rich in Persian and Arabic vocabulary. It developed in northern India from the interaction of local speech with the Persian of the ruling elites.

urf.s: Urf is a term for customary law, and in the Safavid Empire it referred to the royal law administered through the Shah's courts. While Shia judges applied religious law to personal status and family matters, urf handled criminal, commercial and administrative cases that the…

ur-nammu.s: Ur-Nammu was the founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur, or Neo-Sumerian Empire, who established his rule around 2112 BCE after the collapse of the Akkadian Empire. He is credited with the Code of Ur-Nammu, one of the oldest known law codes, and with major building projects…

urshu.s: Urshu was an ancient city in northern Syria or south-eastern Anatolia, besieged by the Hittites during their early expansion. A Hittite text describing the siege provides rare detail on early siege warfare.

uruguay.s: Uruguay is a country in South America on the east bank of the Río de la Plata. In the early nineteenth century the territory, then known as the Cisplatine Province, was contested between Brazil and Argentina, and the costly war over it ended with Uruguayan independence in 1828.

uruk.s: Uruk was one of the oldest and largest cities of ancient Sumer, in southern Mesopotamia, and is associated with the early development of writing and urban life. It was the city of the legendary king Gilgamesh.

ur-zababa.s: Ur-Zababa was a king of the Sumerian city of Kish in the late third millennium BCE. According to tradition, the future Sargon of Akkad served as his cupbearer.

us-oil-embargo-against-japan.s: The US oil embargo against Japan was the cutting off of American oil exports to Japan in 1941, imposed in response to Japanese expansion in Indochina. Accounts of the Empire of Japan note that Japan imported approximately eighty percent of its oil from the United States.

usman-dan-fodio.s: Usman dan Fodio was a Fulani Islamic scholar and reformer who led a jihad against the Hausa kingdoms beginning in 1804 and founded the Sokoto Caliphate. His movement created one of the largest states in nineteenth-century Africa and inspired other reform movements across West…

uss-missouri.s: The USS Missouri was a United States Navy battleship of the Iowa class, commissioned during the Second World War. On 2 September 1945 the formal Japanese surrender was signed aboard it in Tokyo Bay.

uthman-ibn-affan.s: Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 644 to 656 CE. His reign saw continued expansion and the compilation of a standard text of the Quran, but accusations of favouring his Umayyad kinsmen provoked growing discontent.

uyghurs.s: The Uyghurs are a Turkic people who founded a powerful khaganate on the Mongolian steppe in the mid-eighth century after overthrowing the Second Turkic Khaganate in alliance with others. The Uyghur Khaganate became a major ally of the Tang Dynasty before its collapse in 840.

uzama.s: The uzama were the hereditary noble chiefs of the Benin kingdom, who held significant power under the earlier Ogiso system. Accounts of the Benin Empire describe how the Oba dynasty centralised royal authority against them, and how Oba Ewuare the Great removed the uzama…

uzbekistan.s: Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia covering much of historic Transoxiana, including the cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Tashkent. It was the heartland of the Timurid Empire, whose capital was Samarkand, and an important part of the Chagatai Empire.

uzbeks.s: The Uzbeks are a Turkic people of Central Asia whose name derives from the nomadic confederation that formed in the fifteenth century. Under Muhammad Shaybani they conquered Transoxiana from the Timurids around 1500, ending Timurid rule there and driving Babur south.

uzun-hasan.s: Uzun Hasan was the ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen confederation, who died in 1478. He built a powerful state in eastern Anatolia, Iraq and western Iran but was defeated by the Ottomans at Otlukbeli in 1473.

ui-neill.s: The Uí Néill were a group of Irish dynasties claiming descent from Niall of the Nine Hostages. The northern branches ruled Ailech and Tír Eoghain and Tír Chonaill, and the southern branches ruled Mide and Brega.

upper-burma.s: Upper Burma is the inland, northern part of Myanmar around the middle Irrawaddy, including the dry zone where Pagan, Ava and Mandalay stood. It was the heartland of most Burmese kingdoms, in contrast to the Mon country of Lower Burma.

upper-lusatia.s: Upper Lusatia is a historical region on the upper Spree and Neisse, centred on Bautzen and Görlitz, today divided between Germany and Poland. Settled by the Sorbs, it was long held by the Bohemian crown, while its six leading towns formed the Lusatian League in 1346.

union-of-utrecht.s: The Union of Utrecht was an alliance signed in January 1579 by the northern provinces of the Netherlands, led by Holland and Zeeland, to fight together against Spanish rule. It promised mutual defence and freedom of conscience.

upper-silesia.s: Upper Silesia is the south-eastern part of Silesia, on the upper Oder, today mostly in Poland with a part in the Czech Republic. In the Middle Ages it was divided among Piast duchies such as Opole, Racibórz, Bytom and Cieszyn, which came under the Bohemian crown.

uberto-pallavicino.s: Uberto Pallavicino was a Lombard nobleman and leader of the Ghibelline party, a supporter of Emperor Frederick II. From the 1250s he was lord of Cremona, Piacenza and other cities, and briefly of Milan.

udaybhan-singh.s: Udaybhan Singh was the last ruling Maharaj Rana of Dholpur, a Jat princely state in Rajputana, from 1911. He acceded to India in 1947, and in 1948 he became Rajpramukh of the Matsya Union, formed from Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli, before it merged into Rajasthan in 1949.

uesugi-kagekatsu.s: Uesugi Kagekatsu was the adopted heir of Uesugi Kenshin, who won the succession war after Kenshin's death in 1578. Under Toyotomi Hideyoshi he was moved to Aizu with large holdings.

uesugi-kenshin.s: Uesugi Kenshin was a warlord of Echigo province in the Sengoku period, famous for his generalship and Buddhist devotion. He fought Takeda Shingen in five battles at Kawanakajima between 1553 and 1564 and campaigned repeatedly against the Later Hojo in the Kanto.

umar-ibn-hafsun.s: Umar ibn Hafsun was a muwallad rebel who led a long revolt against the Umayyad Emirate of Córdoba from his mountain fortress of Bobastro in southern al-Andalus. He drew support from converts and Christians, allied with other rebels such as the lords of Seville, and is said to…

umur-bey.s: Umur Bey was ruler of the Aydinid beylik in western Anatolia from 1334. From Smyrna his fleets raided the Aegean islands and Greek coasts, and he allied with the Byzantine John VI Kantakouzenos.

upper-march.s: The Upper March was the north-eastern frontier province of al-Andalus, facing the Franks and the Christian kingdoms of the Pyrenees, with its capital at Zaragoza. Local dynasties such as the Banu Qasi of Tudela and later the Tujibids dominated it.

ural-river.s: The Ural River, historically the Yaik, flows from the southern Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea and is often taken as a boundary between Europe and Asia. Its steppes were grazing lands of the White Horde and the Nogai Horde, whose capital Saraychik stood on it.

united-states-declaration-of-independenc.s: The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Second Continental Congress in Philadelphia on 4 July 1776. Drafted mainly by Thomas Jefferson, it announced that the thirteen American colonies were independent states no longer bound to Britain, listed…

ugyen-wangchuck.s: Ugyen Wangchuck was the first hereditary king of Bhutan, elected by an assembly of clergy, officials and leading families at Punakha in 1907. As penlop of Trongsa he defeated his rivals in the civil wars of the late 19th century and won British favour by helping the…

ukit-kan-lek-tok.s: Ukit Kan Le'k Tok' was a Maya king of Ek' Balam in north-eastern Yucatán who took power in 770 and made the city the capital of a regional kingdom, Talol. He died around 801 and was buried in the great Acropolis, in a tomb behind a stucco facade shaped as the jaws of a monster…

ulugh-muhammad.s: Ulugh Muhammad was a Chinggisid khan of the Golden Horde who, after losing power in the struggles of the early 15th century, moved to the middle Volga and around 1438 founded the Khanate of Kazan. He defeated and captured Vasily II of Moscow at Suzdal in 1445, the year he was…

umar-al-aqta.s: Umar al-Aqta was emir of Melitene, a frontier emirate on the upper Euphrates, from about 830 to 863 and one of the most dangerous Arab raiders of Byzantine Anatolia. Allied with the Paulicians of Tephrike, he sacked Amisos on the Black Sea in 863, but was trapped and killed…

umar-walasma.s: Umar Walasma was the founder of the Walashma dynasty and of the Sultanate of Ifat in the eastern highlands of Shewa, Ethiopia. Claiming Arab descent, he conquered the old Sultanate of Shewa in 1285 and absorbed it, creating a Muslim state on the trade routes between the…

umaru-dallaji.s: Umaru Dallaji was a Fulani scholar and follower of Usman dan Fodio who led the jihad in Katsina, capturing the city from its Hausa ruler in 1807. He became the first emir of Katsina within the Sokoto Caliphate, ruling until his death in 1835 and founding the Dallazawa dynasty.

united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.n: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.s: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland was the state created on 1 January 1801 by the Acts of Union, which merged the Kingdom of Great Britain and the Kingdom of Ireland under one parliament at Westminster. It ruled the largest empire of the 19th century.

united-states-military-government-of-the.n: United States Military Government of the Philippine Islands
united-states-military-government-of-the.s: The United States Military Government of the Philippine Islands was the American military administration of the Philippines from the capture of Manila in August 1898. Under a series of military governors it fought the Philippine–American War against the First Philippine Republic.

united-states-military-government-in-cub.n: United States Military Government in Cuba
united-states-military-government-in-cub.s: The United States Military Government in Cuba ruled the island from 1 January 1899, after Spain gave it up at the end of the Spanish–American War, until 20 May 1902. Under the governors John R.

upper-bavaria.s: Upper Bavaria is the southern and south-eastern part of Bavaria, around Munich, Ingolstadt and the Alpine foothills. It emerged as a separate duchy in the Wittelsbach partition of 1255, when Louis II the Strict received it with Munich as his residence, and the duchies of…

uzbek-khan.s: Uzbek Khan was khan of the Golden Horde from 1313 to 1341, the longest reign in its history. He made Islam the state religion, built mosques in the capital Sarai and kept close ties with Mamluk Egypt.

ugandan-bush-war.s: The Ugandan Bush War was the guerrilla war waged by Yoweri Museveni's National Resistance Army against the second government of Milton Obote and then the military regime of Tito Okello. Fighting centred on the Luwero Triangle north of Kampala, where many civilians were killed.

university-of-greifswald.s: The University of Greifswald is a university in the Baltic town of Greifswald in Pomerania, north-eastern Germany, founded in 1456 with the support of Duke Wartislaw IX and the burgomaster Heinrich Rubenow. It became Lutheran during the Reformation.

udai-singh-of-marwar.s: Udai Singh, known as Mota Raja, was the Rathore ruler of Marwar (Jodhpur) from 1583 to 1595, restored to his kingdom as a vassal of Akbar. His daughter married Prince Salim, the future Jahangir, and was the mother of Shah Jahan.

ubashi-khan.s: Ubashi Khan was the last khan of the Kalmyk Khanate on the lower Volga, ruling from 1761. Resenting Russian settlement, Cossack encroachment and interference in Kalmyk affairs, in January 1771 he led about 150,000 Kalmyks east across the Kazakh steppe towards Dzungaria.

udai-singh-of-dungarpur.s: Rawal Udai Singh was ruler of Vagad, with his capital at Dungarpur in southern Rajasthan, in the early 16th century. An ally of Rana Sanga of Mewar, he was killed fighting the Mughal emperor Babur at the Battle of Khanwa in 1527.

udai-singh-of-kaithal.s: Bhai Udai Singh was the last ruler of Kaithal, a Sikh chiefship of the Cis-Sutlej region in present-day Haryana that had accepted British protection in 1809. When he died childless in 1843, the British East India Company annexed most of the state as a lapsed territory and put…

udayana-warmadewa.s: Udayana Warmadewa was a king of Bali of the Warmadewa dynasty in the late 10th and early 11th centuries, ruling from the region of Bedulu. He married the Javanese princess Mahendradatta, and the royal couple issued joint charters.

udayana-of-vatsa.s: Udayana was a king of Vatsa, with its capital at Kaushambi on the Yamuna, in the 6th century BCE, a contemporary of the Buddha. Buddhist texts and Sanskrit drama make him a romantic hero: his capture by King Pradyota of Avanti and his elopement with Pradyota's daughter…

uesugi-harunori.s: Uesugi Harunori, also known as Uesugi Yōzan, was daimyo of the Yonezawa Domain in northern Japan from 1767 to 1785. Facing near bankruptcy, he cut expenses, encouraged sericulture, weaving, lacquer trees and carp ponds, reclaimed land and revived the domain school, the Kōjōkan.

uhtred-the-bold.s: Uhtred the Bold was earl of Bamburgh and, from about 1006, of all Northumbria until his death in 1016. He won fame by defeating a Scottish army besieging Durham in 1006 and was rewarded by King Æthelred the Unready, whose daughter he married.

ui-dunlainge.s: The Uí Dúnlainge were a dynasty of north Leinster, in the plains of modern Kildare, descended from Dúnlaing mac Énda Niada. From the 8th to the 11th century they held the kingship of Leinster almost without break, rotating it between three branches, the Uí Muiredaig, Uí…

ukrainian-soviet-republic.s: The Ukrainian Soviet Republic was a short-lived Bolshevik state proclaimed in March 1918 by merging the Ukrainian People's Republic of Soviets with the other Soviet republics set up in Ukraine, including those of Odessa and Donetsk–Krivoy Rog. Formed as German and…

ulick-de-burgh.s: Ulick de Burgh was the founder of the Clanricarde Burkes of south Galway. After the murder of his kinsman William Donn de Burgh, Earl of Ulster, in 1333, he seized the family's lands in southern Connacht and took the Gaelic title Mac William Uachtar, ruling from Loughrea.

ulick-fionn-burke.s: Ulick Fionn Burke was Mac William Uachtar, lord of Clanricarde in south Galway, from 1485 until his death in 1509. In 1504 he led an alliance with the O'Briens and other Gaelic lords against Gerald FitzGerald, 8th Earl of Kildare, the Lord Deputy of Ireland, and was heavily…

ulises-heureaux.s: Ulises Heureaux was a Dominican general and dictator who dominated the Dominican Republic from 1882 until his assassination in 1899. A hero of the War of Restoration against Spain and a leader of Gregorio Luperón's Blue Party, he became president in 1882 and ruled almost…

ulric-manfred-ii.s: Ulric Manfred II was margrave of Turin from about 1000 until his death in 1034, of the Arduinici family. He controlled the Alpine routes over the Mont Cenis and Mont Genèvre passes, extended the march across much of western Piedmont and founded monasteries, including San…

ulrich-duke-of-mecklenburg.s: Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg, was administrator of the Prince-Bishopric of Schwerin from 1550 and ruled Mecklenburg-Güstrow from 1555 until his death in 1603. A Lutheran prince, he introduced the Reformation in the bishopric, which in practice became an appanage of the…

ulugh-khan.s: Ulugh Khan was a general of the Delhi Sultanate and a brother of Sultan Alauddin Khalji. With Nusrat Khan he invaded Gujarat in 1299, sacking Anahilavada and the temple of Somnath and forcing the Vaghela king Karna to flee.

uluj-ali.s: Uluj Ali was an Italian-born Ottoman corsair and admiral, born in Calabria as Giovanni Dionigi Galeni and captured by Barbary corsairs as a young man. Converting to Islam, he rose to be beylerbey of Algiers from 1568.

umar-al-mutawakkil.s: Umar al-Mutawakkil was the last Aftasid ruler of the Taifa of Badajoz, from about 1067 until 1094, and a noted poet whose court attracted writers. Pressed by Alfonso VI of Castile and fearing the Almoravids, he ceded Lisbon, Sintra and Santarém to Castile in 1093 in return for…

umar-ibn-abd-al-aziz-al-habbari.s: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Habbari was the founder of the Habbari dynasty of Sindh. From an Arab family settled in the province since the conquest, he made himself ruler around 854 at al-Mansura, the provincial capital, as Abbasid authority weakened, while continuing to recognise…

umar-ibn-awad-al-quaiti.s: Umar ibn Awad al-Qu'aiti was the founder of the fortunes of the Qu'aiti family of Hadramawt in southern Arabia. A Yafa'i tribesman, he rose to high rank as a jamadar, or commander, of the Arab troops of the Nizam of Hyderabad in India.

umaru-nagwamatse.s: Umaru Nagwamatse was the founder of the Kontagora Emirate in western Nigeria. A son of the Sokoto caliph Abubakar Atiku and a grandson of Usman dan Fodio, he left Sokoto with followers and around 1859 began conquering lands among the Kamuku, Gbagyi and other peoples between…

umma-khan-v.s: Umma Khan V, called the Great, was khan of Avar in mountainous Dagestan from 1774 until his death in 1801, when the khanate was at the height of its power. He led raids deep into Georgia and Shirvan and received tribute and payments from neighbouring rulers, including the…

united-nations-general-assembly.s: The United Nations General Assembly is the main deliberative body of the United Nations, in which every member state has one vote. First meeting in London in January 1946, it debates international questions, approves the budget and admits members on the Security Council's…

united-nations-security-council.s: The United Nations Security Council is the organ of the United Nations responsible for international peace and security, with power to impose sanctions and authorise force by binding decisions. It has five permanent members with a veto, China, France, Russia (formerly the…

united-fruit-company.s: The United Fruit Company was an American corporation, founded in 1899, that dominated banana growing and trade in Central America and the Caribbean. Owning vast lands, railways and ports, it wielded great political influence, especially in Guatemala, where dictators such as…

united-republic-of-tanganyika-and-zanzib.n: United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar
united-republic-of-tanganyika-and-zanzib.s: The United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar was the union formed on 26 April 1964 by Tanganyika under Julius Nyerere and the People's Republic of Zanzibar under Abeid Karume, a few months after the Zanzibar Revolution. Zanzibar kept its own president and government for…

united-workers-party-saint-lucia.s: The United Workers Party is one of the two main political parties of Saint Lucia, founded in 1964 and led for decades by John Compton. It governed when Saint Lucia became an associated state of Britain in 1967 and led it to independence in 1979, with Compton as the first prime…

university-of-chicago.s: The University of Chicago is a private research university in Chicago, founded in 1890 with funding from John D. Rockefeller.

university-of-tubingen.s: The University of Tübingen was founded in 1477 by Count Eberhard V of Württemberg, called the Bearded, in his town of Tübingen. It became the university of the Duchy of Württemberg and, after the duchy adopted the Reformation in 1534, a centre of Lutheran theology.

upper-alsace.s: Upper Alsace is the southern part of Alsace, between the Vosges, the Rhine and the Swiss frontier, roughly the modern department of Haut-Rhin. In the Middle Ages much of it was held by the Habsburgs, while towns such as Colmar and Mulhouse were imperial cities and members of…

upper-austria.s: Upper Austria is a historical land of the Habsburg monarchy along the Danube west of the Enns river, with Linz as its capital, and is now one of Austria's federal states. Known in the Middle Ages as the land above the Enns, it gradually became a separate land from Lower Austria.

upper-hungary.s: Upper Hungary is the historical name for the northern part of the Kingdom of Hungary, roughly modern Slovakia and parts of north-eastern Hungary, with towns such as Kassa (Košice) and Pozsony (Bratislava). Its mining towns produced silver and gold.

upper-nubia.s: Upper Nubia is the southern part of Nubia, along the Nile in modern Sudan from the Second Cataract southwards. It was the heartland of Kush: the kingdom of Kerma flourished at the Third Cataract from about 2500 BCE, and later Napata and Meroë lay further upstream.

upper-swabia.s: Upper Swabia is the region of south-western Germany between the Danube, the Iller and Lake Constance, in modern Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria. In the Holy Roman Empire it was divided among many small territories, including imperial abbeys such as Weingarten, imperial cities…

uriah-butler.s: Tubal Uriah 'Buzz' Butler was a Grenadian-born labour leader and preacher in Trinidad. A former oilfield worker, he led the oilfield strike of June 1937, which spread into unrest across Trinidad and Tobago and led to the recognition of trade unions and labour reforms.

urien-rheged.s: Urien Rheged was a king of Rheged in northern Britain in the late 6th century, praised in poems attributed to Taliesin. The Historia Brittonum records him leading a coalition of British kings that besieged the Angles of Bernicia on Lindisfarne, before he was murdered at the…

urus-khan.s: Urus Khan was a Jochid ruler of the White Horde, in the eastern part of the Golden Horde, from about 1368 until his death in 1377. He sought to reunite the Golden Horde and briefly held its capital Sarai, but was challenged by Tokhtamysh, who was backed by Timur.

usatges-of-barcelona.s: The Usatges of Barcelona are a collection of customary laws of Catalonia, traditionally attributed to Count Ramon Berenguer I of Barcelona in the mid-11th century but largely compiled in the 12th. They dealt with feudal relations, the keeping of the peace and the authority of…

usman-zaki.s: Usman Zaki was the first emir of Bida in the Nupe country of central Nigeria. A son of the Fulani cleric Mallam Dendo, he became ruler of the Fulani-led Nupe state in the 1830s, was driven out by rivals and then restored with support from Gwandu around 1856, when Bida became…

uthman-dey.s: Uthman Dey was dey of Ottoman Tunisia from 1598 until his death in 1610, when deys chosen from the Janissary corps held real power. He organised the administration and the corsair fleet and welcomed Morisco refugees expelled from Spain from 1609, who founded towns and…

udjahorresnet.s: Udjahorresnet was an Egyptian official, physician and priest of Neith at Sais who served the last Saite kings and then the Persian conquerors. His inscribed statue, now in the Vatican Museums, records that he helped Cambyses II compose his pharaonic titles after the conquest…

united-progressive-party-antigua-and-bar.s: The United Progressive Party is a political party of Antigua and Barbuda formed in 1992 by the merger of three opposition parties. Under Baldwin Spencer it won the 2004 election, ending the long rule of the Antigua Labour Party, and governed until 2014.

united-states-capitol.s: The United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., is the seat of the US Congress. William Thornton, a physician born in the British Virgin Islands, won the design competition, and construction began in 1793.

uxama-argaela.s: Uxama Argaela was a town of the Arevaci near modern El Burgo de Osma in the province of Soria, Spain. A Celtiberian stronghold, it became a Roman municipium and later the seat of the bishopric of Osma, which takes its name from it.

umbria.s: Umbria is a landlocked region of central Italy in the Apennines and the upper Tiber valley. It takes its name from the ancient Umbrians, and its hill towns, among them Perugia, Assisi, Spoleto and Orvieto, were long part of the Papal States before joining the Kingdom of Italy…

uhha-ziti.s: Uhha-ziti was the last major king of Arzawa in western Anatolia in the late 14th century BCE. He allied with Ahhiyawa against the Hittites, but Mursili II defeated his forces around 1320 BCE and took his capital, Apasa.

uija-of-baekje.s: Uija was the last king of Baekje, reigning from 641 to 660. He won early victories over Silla, taking some forty fortresses in 642, but in 660 an alliance of Tang China and Silla invaded, defeated his last army at Hwangsanbeol and captured the capital Sabi.

ustase.s: The Ustaše were a Croatian fascist and ultranationalist movement founded by Ante Pavelić in 1929, which used terrorism against the Yugoslav state, including the assassination of King Alexander in 1934. After the Axis invasion in April 1941 they ruled the Independent State of…

uyayna.s: Uyayna is a town in the Najd region of central Saudi Arabia, north-west of Riyadh in Wadi Hanifa. It was the birthplace of the reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, who began his preaching there in the early 1740s under the protection of its ruler Uthman ibn Mu'ammar.

ufa.s: Ufa is the capital of the Republic of Bashkortostan in Russia, at the confluence of the Belaya and Ufa rivers west of the southern Urals. It was founded as a Russian fortress in 1574 and became a centre for governing the Bashkirs and the region's Muslims.

ubud.s: Ubud is a town in Gianyar regency in the uplands of central Bali, Indonesia. It was the seat of a princely family subordinate to the kingdom of Gianyar, whose palace still stands at its centre.

union-miniere-du-haut-katanga.s: Union Minière du Haut Katanga was a Belgian mining company founded in 1906 to exploit the copper of Katanga in the Belgian Congo. It became one of the world's largest producers of copper, cobalt and uranium.

united-democratic-party-belize.s: The United Democratic Party is one of the two main political parties of Belize, formed in 1973 by the merger of opposition groups. It has alternated in power with the People's United Party, governing under Manuel Esquivel in 1984–1989 and 1993–1998 and under Dean Barrow from…

ulaanbaatar.s: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of Mongolia, on the Tuul River. It began in 1639 as a movable monastery for the first Jebtsundamba Khutughtu and settled at its present site in 1778; Europeans called it Urga.

umar-sanda-kyarimi.s: Umar Sanda Kyarimi was Shehu of Borno from 1937 to 1968, ruling from Maiduguri under British colonial rule and into Nigerian independence. As head of the Borno Native Authority he was one of the most influential traditional rulers of Northern Nigeria in the late colonial period.

united-states-virgin-islands.s: The United States Virgin Islands are a group of Caribbean islands east of Puerto Rico, the main ones being Saint Thomas, Saint John and Saint Croix. As the Danish West Indies they were a Danish colony of sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans until emancipation in 1848.

uiryeo-of-buyeo.s: Uiryeo was a king of Buyeo in the late 3rd century. In 285 the Xianbei chief Murong Hui attacked and sacked his kingdom, and Uiryeo took his own life, as recorded in the Book of Jin.

ursus-of-solothurn.s: Ursus of Solothurn is a Christian martyr who, according to tradition, belonged to the Theban Legion and was executed at Solothurn with his companion Victor around 300. Their shrine became the religious centre of the town in the early Middle Ages.

uzhhorod.s: Uzhhorod is a city on the Uzh river in western Ukraine, the administrative centre of Zakarpattia Oblast on the border with Slovakia. Long part of the Kingdom of Hungary, it gave its name to the Union of Uzhhorod of 1646, which brought the region's Orthodox clergy into union…

urnayr.s: Urnayr was a king of Caucasian Albania in the 4th century, remembered as the ruler who made Christianity the religion of his kingdom. Albanian and Armenian tradition links his baptism to the mission of Gregory the Illuminator.

udayasimha-of-jalor.s: Udayasimha was the Chahamana king of Jalor in Rajasthan in the first half of the 13th century and the most powerful ruler of his line. He extended his kingdom over much of Marwar, including Nadol and Mandor, and faced invasions by Iltutmish of the Delhi Sultanate, at first…

udayamati.s: Udayamati was a queen of the Chaulukya king Bhima I of Gujarat in the 11th century. She commissioned the Rani ki Vav at Patan, a monumental stepwell in memory of her husband, richly carved with hundreds of sculptures of Vishnu's avatars and other deities.

udhampur.s: Udhampur is a city in the Jammu division of Jammu and Kashmir, India, and the seat of Udhampur district, on the road from Jammu to Srinagar. It takes its name from Raja Udham Singh, a son of Maharaja Gulab Singh of the Dogra dynasty.

umi-a-liloa.s: ʻUmi-a-Līloa was ruler (aliʻi nui) of the island of Hawaiʻi around 1500, a son of Līloa by a woman of lower rank. After Līloa's death he overthrew his half-brother Hākau and united the island's six districts under a single ruler.

uttaramerur.s: Uttaramerur is a village in Kanchipuram district, Tamil Nadu, India. Inscriptions on its Vaikuntha Perumal temple from the reign of the Chola king Parantaka I, dated around 919–921, set out rules for choosing the members of the village assembly's committees by drawing lots,…

urasoe.s: Urasoe is a city on Okinawa Island, Japan, just north of Naha. Urasoe Castle, on a ridge overlooking the coast, was the seat of the early kings of Chūzan, among them the lines of Eiso and Satto, before Shō Hashi moved the capital to Shuri in the early 15th century.

ulick-na-gceann-burke-1st-earl-of-clanri.n: Ulick na gCeann Burke, 1st Earl of Clanricarde
ulick-na-gceann-burke-1st-earl-of-clanri.s: Ulick na gCeann Burke was the head of the Clanricarde Burkes of south Galway and the first Earl of Clanricarde. In 1543, under Henry VIII's policy of surrender and regrant, he gave up his lands and Gaelic lordship to the crown and received them back with an English earldom.

ulick-burke-1st-marquess-of-clanricarde.s: Ulick Burke, 1st Marquess of Clanricarde, was an Irish Catholic nobleman who stayed loyal to Charles I during the Irish Confederate Wars. He succeeded as 5th Earl of Clanricarde in 1635 and was made a marquess in 1646.

utila.s: Utila is the smallest of the three main Bay Islands of Honduras, in the western Caribbean near the southern end of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef. English-speaking settlers from the Cayman Islands arrived in the 1830s, and it was part of the British Colony of the Bay Islands…

ulrich-i-count-of-east-frisia.n: Ulrich I, Count of East Frisia
ulrich-i-count-of-east-frisia.s: Ulrich Cirksena was a Frisian chieftain who, after a century of feuds among the chiefs of East Frisia, brought most of the region under his rule. In 1464 Emperor Frederick III made him an imperial count, founding the County of East Frisia and the Cirksena dynasty, which ruled…

upper-rhenish-circle.s: The Upper Rhenish Circle was one of the Imperial Circles of the Holy Roman Empire, created in 1500 to organise defence, taxation and the keeping of the peace. It grouped many small territories along the middle and upper Rhine and in Hesse, including Hesse-Kassel,…

unna.s: Unna is a town in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, at the eastern edge of the Ruhr, east of Dortmund. A town of the County of the Mark and a member of the Hanseatic League, it prospered from the salt works of nearby Königsborn and from trade on the Hellweg road.

usingen.s: Usingen is a small town in the Hochtaunus district of Hesse, Germany, in the Taunus hills north of Frankfurt. From 1659 it was the residence of the counts and later princes of Nassau-Usingen, who built a palace there before moving their court to Biebrich near Wiesbaden in the…

ulrich-i-count-of-wurttemberg.s: Ulrich I, Count of Württemberg, known as the Founder, ruled Württemberg from about 1241 to 1265. In 1246 he deserted the Hohenstaufen king Conrad IV, and as Hohenstaufen power collapsed he acquired many former royal and ducal lands and rights in Swabia, including Urach.

ulrich-of-augsburg.s: Saint Ulrich of Augsburg was bishop of Augsburg from 923 to 973. He organised the defence of the city against the Hungarians in 955, holding out until King Otto I defeated them at the Battle of Lechfeld.

ulrich-duke-of-wurttemberg.s: Ulrich, Duke of Württemberg, ruled from 1498 to 1550. His heavy taxes provoked the Poor Conrad revolt of 1514, and after he seized the imperial city of Reutlingen in 1519 the Swabian League drove him out, leaving the duchy under Habsburg rule.

ua-faelain.s: The Ua Fáeláin were the ruling family of the Déisi of Munster, in what is now County Waterford and south Tipperary, in the 11th and 12th centuries. They took their name from an ancestor called Fáelán.

uperi.s: Uperi was a king of Dilmun in the late 8th century BCE, known from the inscriptions of the Assyrian king Sargon II. Sargon recorded that Uperi, who lived 'like a fish' in the middle of the sea, sent him gifts after the Assyrian conquest of Babylonia in 709 BCE.

united-national-party.s: The United National Party is a political party of Sri Lanka, founded in 1946 by D. S.

university-of-vienna.s: The University of Vienna was founded in 1365 by Duke Rudolf IV of Austria and is the oldest university in today's German-speaking world. A papal bull approved most faculties at the start, and a faculty of theology was added in 1384.

university-of-ingolstadt.s: The University of Ingolstadt was founded in 1472 by Duke Louis IX the Rich of Bavaria-Landshut as the first university in Bavaria. During the Reformation it became a centre of Catholic theology, where Johann Eck taught, and later a Jesuit stronghold.

ukrainians.s: Ukrainians are an East Slavic people whose homeland is Ukraine. Long divided between Poland-Lithuania, Russia and the Habsburg monarchy, they developed a national movement in the 19th century, strongest in Austrian Galicia.

upper-guelders.s: Upper Guelders was the southern quarter of the Duchy of Guelders, around Roermond, Venlo and Geldern on the Meuse and the lower Rhine. Unlike the northern quarters, it stayed with Spain during the Dutch Revolt.

university-of-halle.s: The University of Halle was founded in 1694 by Elector Frederick III of Brandenburg in the Duchy of Magdeburg. Under Christian Thomasius, August Hermann Francke and later Christian Wolff it became a leading centre of Pietism and the early Enlightenment.

university-of-rostock.s: The University of Rostock, founded in 1419 in the Hanseatic city of Rostock with papal approval, is one of the oldest universities in Germany and the oldest in the Baltic Sea region. In the late Middle Ages it drew students from across Scandinavia and the Baltic, and after the…

ulrich-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg-stargard.s: Ulrich II (d. 1471) was the last Duke of Mecklenburg-Stargard, a branch of the Mecklenburg dynasty that had ruled the south-eastern Lordship of Stargard since 1352.

university-of-konigsberg.s: The University of Königsberg, known as the Albertina, was founded in 1544 by Duke Albert of Prussia as a Lutheran university. It became a leading centre of learning in north-eastern Europe, where Immanuel Kant studied and taught.

university-of-jena.s: The University of Jena is a university in Jena, Thuringia, founded by the Ernestine dukes of Saxony and inaugurated in 1558 after they lost Wittenberg. Shared by the Ernestine duchies, it flourished around 1800, when Fichte, Schelling, Hegel and Schiller taught there and the…

union-of-horodlo.s: The Union of Horodło was a set of acts signed at Horodło on the Bug on 2 October 1413 by King Władysław II Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas. It renewed the union of Poland and Lithuania while keeping a separate Lithuanian grand duke.

uraiyur.s: Uraiyur was the inland capital of the early Chola kings in the Sangam age, now a district of the city of Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu, India. Sangam poems describe it as a fortified city, and it was known for its cotton cloth.

university-of-gottingen.s: The University of Göttingen, officially the Georg-August-Universität, is a public university in Lower Saxony, Germany, founded in 1734 by George II of Great Britain as Elector of Hanover and opened in 1737. An Enlightenment foundation with a large library and freedom of…

university-of-wittenberg.s: The University of Wittenberg was founded in 1502 by Frederick the Wise, Elector of Saxony, in his residence town on the Elbe. Martin Luther taught theology there from 1512 and Philip Melanchthon from 1518, making it the intellectual centre of the Protestant Reformation.

ubaid-period.s: The Ubaid period is a prehistoric period of Mesopotamia, from about 6500 to 3800 BCE, named after Tell al-Ubaid near Ur. Farming villages spread across southern Mesopotamia, using irrigation and producing distinctive painted pottery, and the first temples, as at Eridu, appeared.

uromi.s: Uromi is a town in Edo State in southern Nigeria and one of the largest of the Esan chiefdoms, ruled by its own Onojie. Like other Esan chiefdoms it traced its ruling house to the Kingdom of Benin while largely running its own affairs.

ubiaja.s: Ubiaja is a town in Edo State in southern Nigeria, the headquarters of the Esan South-East local government area. It was one of the Esan chiefdoms whose rulers, the Enijie, traced their descent to princes and nobles of the Kingdom of Benin and owed allegiance to the Oba while…

united-malays-national-organisation.s: The United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) is a Malay nationalist party founded in 1946 under Onn Jaafar to oppose the British Malayan Union plan. Under Tunku Abdul Rahman it formed the Alliance with the Malayan Chinese Association and the Malayan Indian Congress, which…

union-of-the-peoples-of-cameroon.n: Union of the Peoples of Cameroon
union-of-the-peoples-of-cameroon.s: The Union of the Peoples of Cameroon (UPC) is a Cameroonian political party founded in 1948 under Ruben Um Nyobe. It demanded independence for French Cameroon and reunification with the British Cameroons.

upstalsboom.s: The Upstalsboom is a burial mound near Aurich in East Frisia, Germany, which served in the Middle Ages as the meeting place of delegates of the Frisian Seven Sealands. Representatives of the free Frisian lands gathered there to settle disputes and agree common laws, and a…

university-of-freiburg.s: The University of Freiburg is a public university in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany, founded in 1457 by Archduke Albert VI of Austria, then ruler of Further Austria. One of the oldest universities in Germany, it remained Catholic during the Reformation and passed to Baden in 1805.

ussher-fort.s: Ussher Fort is a fort in Accra, Ghana, built by the Dutch West India Company in 1649 as Fort Crèvecoeur. It was a base for Dutch trade, including the slave trade, near the English James Fort and the Danish Christiansborg.

ureuk.s: Ureuk was a musician of the Gaya kingdom of Daegaya in 6th-century Korea. According to the Samguk sagi, he composed twelve pieces for the gayageum, the zither devised under King Gasil.

uqair.s: Uqair is a historic port on the Gulf coast of eastern Saudi Arabia, in the al-Ahsa region. For centuries it served as the harbour of the al-Ahsa oasis, and its fort and customs buildings survive.

uqair-protocol.s: The Uqair Protocol of 1922 set the borders between the Sultanate of Nejd under Ibn Saud and the British-protected Kuwait and mandated Iraq. Imposed at a conference at the port of Uqair by the British high commissioner Sir Percy Cox, it gave Nejd about two-thirds of the land…

ugeo-of-gojoseon.s: Ugeo was the last king of Wiman Joseon, the final phase of Gojoseon, and a grandson of its founder Wiman. His control of trade between the Han dynasty and the states of southern Korea and his refusal to submit led Emperor Wu of Han to invade in 109 BCE.

upper-hesse.s: Upper Hesse is a historical region of central Hesse in Germany, around Giessen and the Vogelsberg hills. From the early nineteenth century until 1937 it was one of the three provinces of the Grand Duchy and then the People's State of Hesse, with Giessen as its seat, separated…

uss-charleston-c-2.s: USS Charleston was a protected cruiser of the United States Navy, commissioned in 1889. In June 1898, during the Spanish–American War, she entered Apra Harbour on Guam and fired on the old fort; the Spanish governor, unaware that war had been declared, surrendered the island…

utu-hengal.s: Utu-hengal was a king of Uruk in the late 22nd century BCE who led the Sumerian cities against the Gutians. His victory over the Gutian king Tirigan ended Gutian rule in Sumer, and he took the title 'king of the four quarters'.

urhilina.s: Urhilina, called Irhuleni in Assyrian records, was king of Hamath in the mid-9th century BCE. He joined Hadadezer of Aram-Damascus and Ahab of Israel in the coalition that fought the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III at the Battle of Qarqar in 853 BCE, and the coalition resisted…

udabhandapura.s: Udabhandapura, modern Hund in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, was a city on the right bank of the Indus above Attock, at a main crossing of the river. It became the capital of the Hindu Shahi kings after they lost Kabul in the late 9th century, and Alexander the Great…

una-river.s: The Una is a river of the western Balkans, a right tributary of the Sava, which for much of its course forms the border between Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. It flows past Bihać and is known for its clear water and waterfalls, protected in Una National Park.

una-himachal-pradesh.s: Una is a town in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, headquarters of the district of the same name, near the border with Punjab. It lies in the valley of the Swan, or Sohan, a tributary of the Sutlej.

university-of-al-qarawiyyin.s: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco, began as a mosque founded in 859 by Fatima al-Fihri. Rebuilt and enlarged under later dynasties, it became one of the leading centres of Islamic learning in North Africa, teaching law, theology, grammar and the sciences.

ulrich-rosch.s: Ulrich Rösch was abbot of Saint Gall from 1463 until his death in 1491, after serving as its administrator from 1457. A baker's son, he restored the abbey's finances, bought the County of Toggenburg in 1468 and built a strong territorial state in eastern Switzerland.

uppsala.s: Uppsala is a city in eastern Sweden, north of Stockholm. Nearby Old Uppsala, with its royal burial mounds, was a centre of the pre-Christian kings of the Swedes and of a pagan temple described by Adam of Bremen.

ullastret.s: Ullastret is an archaeological site in the Baix Empordà in Catalonia, the largest known Iberian settlement in the region and the chief town of the Indigetes. Occupied from the 6th century BCE, it had stone walls with towers, temples and grain silos, and its buildings and…

ubayd-zakani.s: Ubayd Zakani was a Persian poet and satirist from Qazvin, active in Shiraz in the 14th century. He enjoyed the patronage of the Injuid ruler Abu Ishaq.

university-of-graz.s: The University of Graz is the second-oldest university in Austria, founded in 1585 by Archduke Charles II of Inner Austria and entrusted to the Jesuits as an instrument of the Counter-Reformation. It was refounded as a state university in the 19th century and named after its…

usain-bolt.s: Usain Bolt is a Jamaican sprinter widely regarded as the greatest of all time. He won the 100 and 200 metres at three successive Olympic Games, 2008, 2012 and 2016, and set world records of 9.58 seconds for 100 metres and 19.19 seconds for 200 metres in Berlin in 2009.

uesugi-zenshu-rebellion.s: The Uesugi Zenshū rebellion was a revolt in the Kanto region of Japan in 1416 and 1417 led by Uesugi Ujinori, known as Zenshū, a former deputy of the Kamakura kubo. Allied with discontented warriors, he drove Ashikaga Mochiuji from Kamakura, but the shogunate sent help, and…

udmurts.s: The Udmurts are a Finno-Ugric people of the lands between the Vyatka and Kama rivers, most of whom live in the Udmurt Republic of Russia, with its capital at Izhevsk. They came under Volga Bulgaria and later the Khanate of Kazan, and most were absorbed into Russia after the…

umar-khan-of-kokand.s: Umar Khan was khan of Kokand from about 1810 to 1822, succeeding his murdered brother Alim Khan. He extended the khanate's rule into the steppe of the Syr Darya, taking the town of Turkestan, and Kokand built forts along the river.

urmia.s: Urmia is a city in north-western Iran, the capital of West Azerbaijan province, on a plain west of Lake Urmia. Long home to Muslims alongside Assyrian and Armenian Christians, it was a centre of Christian missions in the 19th century.

uqba-ibn-nafi.s: Uqba ibn Nafi was an Arab general of the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates who led the conquest of North Africa. He founded Kairouan in Ifriqiya around 670 as a base for campaigns against the Berbers and Byzantines, and in a later expedition reportedly reached the Atlantic coast.

ui-briuin-breifne.s: The Uí Briúin Bréifne were a branch of the Uí Briúin dynasty of Connacht that settled the lakes and hills of later Leitrim and Cavan and gave their name to the kingdom of Breifne, which emerged in the 8th century. Its leading families were the Ó Ruairc, who usually held the…

ua-conchobair-dynasty.s: The Ua Conchobair, later O'Conor, were a dynasty of the Uí Briúin who ruled the kingdom of Connacht from the 11th century. Two of its kings, Toirdelbach and his son Ruaidrí, claimed the high kingship of Ireland in the 12th century.

ui-briuin.s: The Uí Briúin were a dynastic group of early medieval Connacht, claiming descent from Brión, son of the legendary king Eochaid Mugmedón. From the 8th century they dominated the kingship of Connacht, and their branches included the Uí Briúin Aí, from whom the Ua Conchobair…

ui-fiachrach.s: The Uí Fiachrach were a dynastic group of early medieval Connacht, claiming descent from Fiachrae, son of the legendary king Eochaid Mugmedón. Their branches held lands in the north and west of the province, in later Mayo and Sligo, and in south Galway, and they supplied kings…

university-of-zagreb.s: The University of Zagreb is the oldest and largest university in Croatia. It traces its origins to a Jesuit academy founded in 1669 and was opened as a modern university in 1874, with faculties of law, theology and philosophy, with the support of Bishop Josip Juraj Strossmayer.

united-states-marine-corps.s: The United States Marine Corps is the maritime land force of the United States, founded in 1775 and serving under the Department of the Navy. In the late 19th and early 20th centuries Marines landed repeatedly in the Pacific and the Caribbean, supporting the overthrow of the…

udayin.s: Udayin, or Udayabhadra, was a king of Magadha of the Haryanka dynasty, the son and successor of Ajatashatru. Buddhist and Jain tradition credits him with founding Pataliputra, modern Patna, on the Ganges, which became Magadha's capital and later the capital of the Maurya Empire.

upolu.s: Upolu is the second-largest and most populous island of Samoa, home to the capital Apia. Its high chiefly titles were central to Samoan politics, and in the 19th century Apia became the base of rival German, British and American interests.

upper-navarre.s: Upper Navarre is the part of the Kingdom of Navarre south of the Pyrenees, around Pamplona, which Ferdinand the Catholic conquered in 1512 and joined to the Crown of Castile in 1515. It kept its own laws, cortes and coinage under a viceroy until 1841, when it became a Spanish…

upper-ossory.s: Upper Ossory is the northern part of the old kingdom of Osraige, in what is now County Laois, Ireland. After the Anglo-Norman invasion the Mac Giolla Phádraig (Fitzpatrick) family kept it as their lordship, and in 1541 their chief Brian surrendered it to Henry VIII and…

usora.s: Usora was a medieval region in northern Bosnia, around the valley of the Usora river, a tributary of the Bosna near Doboj. Often grouped with the neighbouring land of Soli under Hungarian overlordship, it was granted in 1284 to Stefan Dragutin of Serbia, and in the 14th…

unstrut.s: The Unstrut is a river of about 190 kilometres in Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, a tributary of the Saale. On its banks the Franks crushed the Thuringian kingdom in 531, and Henry IV defeated the rebel Saxons there in 1075.

uilliam-buidhe-o-ceallaigh.s: Uilliam Buidhe Ó Ceallaigh was king of Uí Maine in Connacht in the mid 14th century. At Christmas 1351 he held a great feast for the poets, historians and musicians of Ireland, celebrated in a poem by Gofraidh Fionn Ó Dálaigh.

ulster-cycle.s: The Ulster Cycle is a body of medieval Irish heroic tales about the Ulaid, their king Conchobar mac Nessa and the warriors of his court at Emain Macha. Its centrepiece is the Táin Bó Cúailnge, the Cattle Raid of Cooley, in which the young hero Cú Chulainn defends Ulster…

university-of-hohenheim.s: The University of Hohenheim is a university in Stuttgart, Germany, housed in and around the 18th-century Hohenheim Palace. It was founded in 1818 by King William I of Württemberg as an agricultural school after the famine of 1816–1817, and it became one of Europe's leading…

uesugi-noritada.s: Uesugi Noritada was the Kantō deputy, or kanrei, the chief adviser of the Kamakura kubo in eastern Japan, from the late 1440s. The son of Uesugi Norizane, who had helped destroy the previous kubo Ashikaga Mochiuji, he was distrusted by Mochiuji's son Shigeuji.

uttarakhand.s: Uttarakhand is a state of northern India in the central Himalaya, with its capital at Dehradun. It was carved out of Uttar Pradesh in 2000 and is made up of the historical regions of Garhwal and Kumaon.

ur-nanshe.s: Ur-Nanshe was the founder of the First Dynasty of Lagash in Sumer around 2500 BCE. His inscriptions record the building of temples and canals, and one notes that ships of Dilmun brought him timber from foreign lands.

urukagina.s: Urukagina, or Uru-inimgina, was the last ruler of the First Dynasty of Lagash, reigning around 2350 BCE. His inscriptions describe reforms that curbed the abuses of officials and priests, cut fees, restored temple property and protected widows and orphans, often cited as the…

university-of-marburg.s: The University of Marburg, in Hesse, Germany, was founded by Landgrave Philip I of Hesse in 1527 and is the oldest Protestant-founded university still in existence. It trained clergy and officials for the Hessian Reformation and was named the Philipps-Universität after its…

university-of-giessen.s: The University of Giessen, in Hesse, Germany, was founded in 1607 by Landgrave Louis V of Hesse-Darmstadt as a Lutheran university, after the University of Marburg had become Calvinist. In the 19th century the chemist Justus von Liebig made it a leading centre of chemistry,…

utu.s: Utu, called Shamash in Akkadian, was the Mesopotamian god of the sun, justice and truth. Each day he crossed the sky and saw all deeds, so he was invoked as judge and as protector of travellers; Hammurabi's law code shows him handing the king authority.

uchchala.s: Uchchala was a king of Kashmir who founded the second Lohara dynasty. With his brother Sussala he rebelled against the tyrannical King Harsha, who was overthrown and killed in 1101.

uzice.s: Užice is a city in western Serbia on the Đetinja river. In the 14th century it was the seat of the regional lord Nikola Altomanović, who was captured there by Prince Lazar and Tvrtko of Bosnia in 1373.

university-of-turin.s: The University of Turin is one of the oldest universities in Italy, founded in 1404 under Prince Louis of Savoy-Achaea with papal approval. It moved several times in its early centuries and was reorganised by Victor Amadeus II in the 1720s as a state university.

unterland-liechtenstein.s: The Unterland is the northern of the two traditional regions of Liechtenstein, corresponding to the former Lordship of Schellenberg. It comprises the five municipalities of Eschen, Gamprin, Mauren, Ruggell and Schellenberg and forms one of the country's two electoral districts.

umm-an-nar-culture.s: The Umm an-Nar culture was a Bronze Age culture of south-eastern Arabia, in modern Oman and the United Arab Emirates, dated about 2600–2000 BCE and named after an island off Abu Dhabi. Its people lived in settlements with round stone towers, buried their dead in large round…

umm-al-quwain.s: Umm al-Quwain is a town on a sandy peninsula of the Gulf coast, capital of the emirate of the same name in the United Arab Emirates. The Al Ali tribe under the Al Mualla family founded it in 1775, and it became one of the Trucial States under British protection before joining…

udayagiri-and-khandagiri-caves.s: The Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves are rock-cut chambers in two neighbouring hills near Bhubaneswar in Odisha, carved mostly in the 1st century BCE as dwellings for Jain monks. Many were excavated under King Kharavela of Kalinga and his queen, and the Hathigumpha ('elephant…

uttar-pradesh.s: Uttar Pradesh is a state of northern India, the most populous in the country, lying across the Ganges–Yamuna plain with its capital at Lucknow. It contains Varanasi, Prayagraj, Ayodhya, Mathura and Agra, and the Buddhist sites of Sarnath and Kushinagar.

ullusunu.s: Ullusunu was a king of Mannaea in north-western Iran in the late 8th century BCE, son of Iranzu. After his brother Aza was killed, he took the throne and at first sided with Rusa I of Urartu, but in 716 BCE he submitted to Sargon II of Assyria, who confirmed him as king.

unruochings.s: The Unruochings were a Frankish noble family named after its early member Unruoch. Eberhard, who married Louis the Pious's daughter Gisela, held the March of Friuli from about 846 and owned a notable library.

usipetes.s: The Usipetes were a Germanic people of the lower Rhine. Driven from their land by the Suebi, they crossed the Rhine with the Tencteri in 55 BCE into the territory of the Menapii, but Julius Caesar defeated them and slaughtered many.

ujiji.s: Ujiji is a town on the eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika in western Tanzania, one of the oldest market towns of the region. In the 19th century it was the lakeside terminus of the caravan route from the Swahili coast through Tabora, through which Arab and Swahili traders…

union-of-united-mountaineers-of-the-nort.n: Union of United Mountaineers of the North Caucasus and Dagestan
union-of-united-mountaineers-of-the-nort.s: The Union of United Mountaineers of the North Caucasus and Dagestan was a political organisation founded at a congress in Vladikavkaz in May 1917, after the February Revolution. It brought together representatives of the Chechens, Ingush, Ossetians, Kabardians, Dagestanis and…

usama-ibn-munqidh.s: Usama ibn Munqidh was an Arab poet, soldier and courtier of the Munqidhite family of Shaizar in northern Syria. He served the rulers of Damascus, the Fatimids in Cairo, and Nur al-Din and Saladin, and had friendly dealings with Frankish knights.

urzana.s: Urzana was king of Musasir, a small mountain state between Assyria and Urartu famous for the temple of the god Haldi. His letters to Sargon II of Assyria survive.

university-of-mysore.s: The University of Mysore is a public university in Mysore, Karnataka, founded in 1916 by Maharaja Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV on the advice of M. Visvesvaraya.

ucanal.s: Ucanal is a Maya archaeological site on the Mopan River in the Petén department of Guatemala. Known in inscriptions as K'anwitznal, it was a regional centre of the Classic period that fought with neighbouring Naranjo, which defeated it in the late 7th century.

undang.s: The Undang are the four great territorial chiefs of Negeri Sembilan in Malaysia, ruling the districts of Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Johol and Rembau. Under the matrilineal adat perpatih customs brought by Minangkabau settlers from Sumatra, they hold the right to choose the state's…

uzun-haji.s: Uzun-Haji was a Naqshbandi sheikh from Dagestan who opposed Russian rule in the North Caucasus and spent years in exile and prison. In September 1919, during the Russian Civil War, he proclaimed the North Caucasian Emirate in the mountains of Chechnya and Dagestan, with…

ulster-unionist-party.s: The Ulster Unionist Party is a unionist political party in Northern Ireland, founded in 1905 as the Ulster Unionist Council to oppose Irish home rule. It governed Northern Ireland without interruption from 1921 to 1972, under leaders such as James Craig and Terence O'Neill.

united-national-independence-party.s: The United National Independence Party (UNIP) is a Zambian political party founded in 1959 and led by Kenneth Kaunda, successor to the banned Zambia African National Congress. It led the campaign against the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland and won the elections of 1964…

uqaylid-dynasty.s: The Uqaylid dynasty was an Arab Shia dynasty of the Banu Uqayl that ruled Mosul and much of northern Iraq and the Jazira from about 990 to 1096. It rose as Buyid and Hamdanid power declined, and its emir Muslim ibn Quraysh extended its rule to Aleppo and Harran in the 1080s.

uzuncaburc.s: Uzuncaburç is a village in Mersin Province in southern Turkey, in the hills above Silifke, on the site of the sanctuary town of ancient Olba, later called Diocaesarea. It grew around the temple of Zeus Olbios, built in the early 3rd century BCE and one of the earliest…

uruguayan-civil-war.s: The Uruguayan Civil War, known as the Guerra Grande, was fought from 1839 to 1851 between the Colorados of Fructuoso Rivera and the Blancos of Manuel Oribe. Oribe was backed by the Argentine ruler Juan Manuel de Rosas, while the Colorados had support at times from Brazil,…

upper-assam.s: Upper Assam is the eastern part of the Brahmaputra valley in the Indian state of Assam, including the districts of Dibrugarh, Tinsukia, Sivasagar, Jorhat and Golaghat. It was the heartland of the Ahom kingdom, whose capitals stood there, and in the nineteenth century it became…

uthumphon.s: Uthumphon was a king of Ayutthaya who succeeded his father Borommakot in 1758 but gave up the throne within weeks to his elder brother Ekkathat and became a monk. When the Burmese took Ayutthaya in 1767 he was carried off to Burma, where he died in 1796; testimony attributed…

ungjin-commandery.s: The Ungjin Commandery was the administration set up by Tang China to govern the former kingdom of Baekje after its conquest in 660. Based at Ungjin (modern Gongju), it was headed for a time by the Baekje prince Buyeo Yung under Tang supervision.

united-nations-emergency-force.s: The United Nations Emergency Force was the first armed peacekeeping force of the United Nations, created in November 1956 on the proposal of Lester B. Pearson to secure the end of the Suez Crisis.

universal-declaration-of-human-rights.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is a statement of fundamental rights and freedoms adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948. Drafted by a commission chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt, from a first draft by John Peters Humphrey, its thirty…

ustertag.s: The Ustertag was a mass assembly of some 10,000 people from the countryside of the canton of Zürich, held at Uster on 22 November 1830. Its Uster Memorial demanded a new constitution with representation according to population and equal rights for town and country.

university-of-cape-town.s: The University of Cape Town is the oldest university in South Africa, founded in 1829 as the South African College, a school for boys in Cape Town. It became a university in 1918, with its main campus on the slopes of Devil's Peak.

utik.s: Utik was a province of ancient Armenia on the right bank of the Kura river, between Artsakh and the river. After the partition of Armenia around 387 it passed to Caucasian Albania, which gained its chief city Partav, later Barda, the Albanian capital from the late fifth century.

union-of-aragon.s: The Union of Aragon was a league of nobles and towns of the Kingdom of Aragon formed in 1283 to defend their privileges against the crown. It forced Peter III to grant the General Privilege of 1283 and Alfonso III the Privileges of the Union in 1287, which allowed resistance…

university-of-alcala.s: The University of Alcalá was founded at Alcalá de Henares, near Madrid, by Cardinal Francisco Jiménez de Cisneros under a papal bull of 1499 and opened in 1508. A centre of Renaissance humanism and theology, it produced the Complutensian Polyglot Bible.

university-of-nantes.s: The University of Nantes was founded in 1460 by Duke Francis II of Brittany with a bull of Pope Pius II, giving the duchy its own university. It taught theology, law, medicine and the arts until the French Revolution closed it in 1793, though its law faculty had moved to…

upper-burgundy.s: Upper Burgundy was a kingdom founded in 888 by the Welf Rudolf I, crowned at Saint-Maurice d'Agaune, covering the lands between the Jura and the Pennine Alps around Lake Geneva and the later Franche-Comté. Around 933 his son Rudolf II united it with Lower Burgundy, the kingdom…

university-of-pont-a-mousson.s: The University of Pont-à-Mousson was founded in 1572 by Duke Charles III of Lorraine and his cousin Cardinal Charles of Lorraine, with papal approval, and was run by the Jesuits. A centre of the Catholic Reformation in Lorraine and the neighbouring lands, it taught theology,…

university-of-pavia.s: The University of Pavia is one of the oldest universities in Europe, founded in 1361 when Emperor Charles IV granted a charter at the request of Galeazzo II Visconti, lord of Pavia. As the university of the Duchy of Milan it trained lawyers, physicians and officials for the…

uckermark.s: The Uckermark is a historical region in the north-east of Brandenburg, Germany, named after the Ucker river, with Prenzlau as its main town. Contested between Pomerania and Brandenburg in the Middle Ages, it was ceded by Barnim I to Brandenburg in the Treaty of Landin of 1250.

usedom.s: Usedom is an island in the Baltic Sea at the mouth of the Oder, divided between Germany and Poland, whose part includes the port of Świnoujście. In 1128 an assembly of Pomeranian nobles at Usedom accepted Christianity under Otto of Bamberg.

u-boat.s: U-boat is the English name for German military submarines, from the German Unterseeboot. In both world wars U-boats waged campaigns against Allied merchant shipping that threatened Britain's supply lines, in 1917 and again in the Battle of the Atlantic of 1939–1945.

upper-volta.s: Upper Volta was a French colony in West Africa created in 1919 from parts of Upper Senegal and Niger, centred on the Mossi kingdoms. It was divided among neighbouring colonies in 1932 and re-formed in 1947.

unsuri.s: Unsuri was a Persian poet from Balkh who became the poet laureate, or king of poets, at the court of Mahmud of Ghazni. He wrote panegyric odes celebrating Mahmud's victories and also verse romances, now mostly lost.

uch-sharif.s: Uch Sharif is a historic town in the southern Punjab of Pakistan, near the confluence of the Chenab and Sutlej rivers. In the thirteenth century it was a political centre of Nasir ad-Din Qabacha and a refuge for scholars fleeing the Mongols, and it became a great centre of…

ugra-river.s: The Ugra is a river of western Russia, about 400 kilometres long, flowing through the Smolensk and Kaluga regions into the Oka. In the fifteenth century it marked part of the border between Muscovy and Lithuania.

uicheon.s: Uicheon was a Korean Buddhist monk of the Goryeo period and the fourth son of King Munjong. After studying in Song China in 1085-1086, he collected Buddhist commentaries from across East Asia and had them printed as a supplement to the Tripitaka.

uijong-of-goryeo.s: Uijong of Goryeo was king of Goryeo from 1146 to 1170. Remembered for his love of pleasure and favour towards civil officials, he provoked resentment among the military.

union-of-brest.s: The Union of Brest was the agreement of 1595-1596 by which most Orthodox bishops of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth accepted the authority of the pope while keeping their Byzantine rite and customs. Confirmed at a synod in Brest in 1596, it created the Ruthenian Uniate Church.

union-of-kedainiai.s: The Union of Kėdainiai was an agreement signed in October 1655 at Kėdainiai in Lithuania by Janusz Radziwiłł and other Lithuanian nobles with Charles X Gustav of Sweden. urbarial-patent-of-1767.s: The Urbarial Patent of 1767 was a decree of Maria Theresa that regulated the obligations of serfs to their lords in the Kingdom of Hungary. Issued after the Hungarian diet failed to act and peasant unrest grew, it fixed the size of peasant holdings and limited labour services,…

university-of-salamanca.s: The University of Salamanca is the oldest university in Spain still operating, founded by Alfonso IX of León in 1218 and granted a royal charter in 1254. united-states-congress.s: The United States Congress is the legislature of the United States, made up of the Senate, with two members from each state, and the House of Representatives, elected by population. uiju.s: Uiju is a town in North Pyongan Province, North Korea, on the Yalu River opposite the Chinese city of Dandong. For centuries it was Korea's main gateway to China, through which tribute missions and trade passed.

uzgen.s: Uzgen is a town in the Osh Region of Kyrgyzstan, in the eastern Fergana Valley. In the eleventh and twelfth centuries it was a capital and royal burial place of the Kara-Khanid dynasty, and a brick minaret and three richly decorated mausoleums from that period survive.

utraquism.s: Utraquism was the moderate branch of the Hussite movement in Bohemia, named after its central demand for communion under both kinds (sub utraque specie), bread and wine, for the laity. Recognised by the Compacts of Basel in 1436, the Utraquist church coexisted with Catholicism…

uganda-peoples-congress.s: The Uganda People's Congress is a political party founded in 1960 under the leadership of Milton Obote. In alliance with Kabaka Yekka it formed Uganda's first government at independence in 1962.

uganda-martyrs.s: The Uganda Martyrs were Christian converts, Catholic and Anglican, killed on the orders of Kabaka Mwanga II of Buganda between 1885 and 1887, many of them young pages at the royal court. The largest group was burned at Namugongo on 3 June 1886.

uraniborg.s: Uraniborg was the observatory and residence built by the astronomer Tycho Brahe on the island of Ven in the Øresund, with the support of Frederick II of Denmark, from 1576. Designed as a Renaissance palace with instruments, a library, workshops and a printing press, it was…

university-of-paris.s: The University of Paris was one of the first universities in Europe, emerging in the twelfth century from the cathedral schools of Paris and receiving royal and papal privileges around 1200. umberto-i.s: Umberto I was King of Italy from 1878 to 1900, the son of Victor Emmanuel II. His reign saw the Triple Alliance with Germany and Austria-Hungary, the first colonial ventures in East Africa and the defeat at Adwa in 1896.

umberto-ii.s: Umberto II was the last King of Italy, reigning for just over a month in 1946. The son of Victor Emmanuel III, he acted as lieutenant-general of the realm from 1944 and became king when his father abdicated on 9 May 1946.

united-kingdom-of-portugal-brazil-and-th.s: The United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves was the monarchy created in December 1815, when the Portuguese court, which had fled to Rio de Janeiro in 1807, raised Brazil from a colony to a kingdom equal with Portugal. union-of-the-crowns.s: The Union of the Crowns was the accession of James VI of Scotland to the thrones of England and Ireland on the death of Elizabeth I in March 1603. university-of-naples-federico-ii.s: The University of Naples Federico II was founded by the emperor Frederick II on 5 June 1224 to train lawyers and administrators for his Kingdom of Sicily, so that his subjects need not study at Bologna. It is the oldest state-founded university in the world still in operation.

university-of-liberia.s: The University of Liberia, in Monrovia, is the country's main public university. It was chartered in 1851 as Liberia College, opened in 1862, and became a university in 1951.

united-states-navy.s: The United States Navy is the naval service of the United States, founded as the Continental Navy in 1775 and re-established under the Naval Act of 1794. In the 19th century its African Squadron patrolled the West African coast to suppress the Atlantic slave trade, and…

uherske-hradiste.s: Uherské Hradiště is a town on the Morava river in south-eastern Moravia, in the Zlín Region of the Czech Republic. It was founded by King Ottokar II of Bohemia around 1257 as a royal town guarding the border with Hungary.

uttarapatha.s: Uttarapatha, 'the northern road', was the ancient trade route of northern India, running from the Ganges plain through Taxila and the north-west towards Bactria and Central Asia. Mentioned in Buddhist and Sanskrit texts, the name was also used for the northern regions it crossed.

united-states-mexico-canada-agreement.s: The United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement (USMCA) is the free trade agreement between the three North American countries that replaced NAFTA. Negotiated at the insistence of the Trump administration and signed in 2018, it came into force on 1 July 2020.

uronarti.s: Uronarti was a Middle Kingdom Egyptian fortress on an island in the Nile near Semna, in Lower Nubia, built under Senusret III. Triangular in plan to fit the island, it was part of the chain of forts guarding Egypt's southern frontier.

uss-buchanan-ddg-14.s: USS Buchanan was a Charles F. Adams-class guided-missile destroyer of the United States Navy, commissioned in 1962.

university-of-chile.s: The University of Chile is Chile's oldest and largest public university, founded in Santiago in 1842 as the successor to the colonial Royal University of San Felipe. Its first rector was Andrés Bello.

university-of-tartu.s: The University of Tartu is the oldest and most prestigious university in Estonia, founded in 1632 by King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden. Reopened in 1802 under Russian rule as a German-language university, it trained scholars from across the Russian Empire.

ulysses-s-grant.s: Ulysses S. Grant was an American general and the 18th president of the United States.

uisang.s: Uisang was a Silla Buddhist monk who went to Tang China in 661 and studied under Zhiyan, a patriarch of the Huayan school. Returning around 670, he founded the Korean Hwaeom school and the temple of Buseoksa in 676.

ulrich-von-jungingen.s: Ulrich von Jungingen was Grand Master of the Teutonic Order from 1407 to 1410. Taking a hard line towards Poland and Lithuania over Samogitia and Dobrzyń Land, he went to war with them in 1409.

umbutfo-eswatini-defence-force.s: The Umbutfo Eswatini Defence Force is the army of Eswatini, formed after independence in 1968. Its name, umbutfo, refers to the traditional Swazi age-regiments from which it draws its identity, and the king is its commander-in-chief.

ulrich-wille.s: Ulrich Wille was a Swiss army officer who served as commander-in-chief, with the rank of general, during the First World War, from 1914 to 1918. He sought to modernise the militia army along Prussian lines of discipline and training.
