ulster-volunteers.s: The Ulster Volunteers were a Unionist militia founded in 1912 and organised in January 1913 as the Ulster Volunteer Force to resist Home Rule for Ireland. Armed with rifles smuggled from Germany in the Larne gun-running of April 1914, they numbered about 100,000 men, and many…

union-flag.s: The Union Flag, or Union Jack, is the national flag of the United Kingdom. Its present form dates from 1 January 1801, when the red saltire of St Patrick, representing Ireland, was added to the crosses of St George for England and St Andrew for Scotland, which had been…

uruk-period.s: The Uruk period is the archaeological period of Mesopotamia from about 4000 to 3100 BCE, named after the city of Uruk. Its later phase saw the growth of the first true cities, monumental temples, the cylinder seal and the earliest proto-cuneiform writing, and an Uruk expansion…

usuthu.s: The uSuthu were the faction of the Zulu royal house loyal to Cetshwayo and later to his son Dinuzulu. The name arose among Cetshwayo's supporters in the succession war of 1856.

university-of-tehran.s: The University of Tehran is the oldest modern university in Iran, founded in 1934 under Reza Shah by bringing together earlier colleges of law, medicine, engineering and teacher training. It became the leading centre of Iranian higher education and a focus of political…

upanishads.s: The Upanishads are philosophical texts in Sanskrit that form the latest layer of the Vedas, the oldest of them composed from around 700 BCE in northern India. Through dialogues between teachers and pupils they explore the identity of the self, atman, with the ultimate reality,…

udaipur.s: Udaipur is a city in southern Rajasthan, India, founded in 1559 by Maharana Udai Singh II as the new capital of Mewar. Built around Lake Pichola and other artificial lakes in the Aravalli hills, it was the seat of the Sisodia Maharanas until 1949, whose City Palace and lake…

udayeshwar-temple.s: The Udayeshwar Temple, also called Neelkantheshwar, is an 11th-century Shiva temple at Udaipur in Vidisha district of Madhya Pradesh, India. Inscriptions attribute it to the Paramara king Udayaditya, who built it between about 1059 and 1080.

utendi-wa-tambuka.s: The Utendi wa Tambuka is an epic poem in Swahili composed in 1728 at the court of Pate, on the coast of present-day Kenya. It tells of a war between the forces of the Prophet Muhammad and the Byzantine Empire at Tabuk, and its manuscript is the oldest dated work of Swahili…

udine.s: Udine is a city in north-eastern Italy and the historic capital of Friuli. From the 13th century it was the main residence of the patriarchs of Aquileia, and after Venice conquered Friuli in 1420 it became the seat of the Venetian lieutenant.

university-of-sydney.s: The University of Sydney, founded in 1850, is the oldest university in Australia. Its main campus at Camperdown in Sydney is known for its Gothic Revival quadrangle.

uncas.s: Uncas was a sachem of the Mohegan in Connecticut. A Pequot noble by birth, he broke away from the Pequot leadership in the 1630s and allied with the English, fighting beside them in the Pequot War of 1637.

uzana-i-of-pinya.s: Uzana I was king of Pinya in central Burma from 1325 to 1340, a son of the Pagan king Kyawswa and stepson of Thihathu, founder of Pinya. Thihathu's son Saw Yun had already broken away to found the rival kingdom of Sagaing in 1315, and Uzana ruled the southern part of the…

unita.s: UNITA, the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola, is an Angolan movement founded in 1966 by Jonas Savimbi, with its strongest support among the Ovimbundu of the central highlands. It fought the Portuguese and then, with South African and United States support,…

university-of-dillingen.s: The University of Dillingen was founded in 1551 by Cardinal Otto Truchsess von Waldburg, prince-bishop of Augsburg, in his residence town of Dillingen on the Danube. Run by the Jesuits from 1563, it trained Catholic clergy for southern Germany and became a stronghold of the…

upper-franconia.s: Upper Franconia is an administrative region in the north-east of Bavaria, Germany, with Bayreuth as its seat. It covers the lands of the former prince-bishopric of Bamberg and the principality of Bayreuth, which passed to Bavaria between 1802 and 1810.

uta-von-ballenstedt.s: Uta von Ballenstedt was a Saxon noblewoman, the wife of Margrave Ekkehard II of Meissen. Her statue by the Naumburg Master in the west choir of Naumburg Cathedral, carved about two centuries after her death, became one of the most celebrated figures of medieval German art.

urup.s: The Urup is a river of the North Caucasus in Russia, about 230 kilometres long, a left tributary of the Kuban. It rises on the northern slopes of the Greater Caucasus in Karachay-Cherkessia and flows north into Krasnodar Krai.

uslar.s: Uslar is a small town in the Solling hills of southern Lower Saxony, Germany, north-west of Göttingen. In the Middle Ages it belonged to the Guelph Principality of Göttingen and later to Calenberg and the Electorate of Hanover.

ujarma.s: Ujarma is a ruined fortress in the Iori valley of eastern Georgia, east of Tbilisi. Tradition credits its fortification to King Vakhtang I Gorgasali in the 5th century, and it served as a royal residence.

ulcinj.s: Ulcinj is a town on the southern Adriatic coast of Montenegro near the Albanian border, with an Albanian majority. An old port, held by Venice and from 1571 by the Ottomans, it was notorious as a base of corsairs.

uglich.s: Uglich is a town on the upper Volga in Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia. Long part of the Rostov lands, it became the seat of its own princes in 1218 and was later absorbed by Moscow.

university-of-helmstedt.s: The University of Helmstedt was founded in 1576 by Duke Julius of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel as a Lutheran university, and for a time it was one of the largest in Germany, known for its theology and humanist learning. Its importance declined in the 18th century, and it was closed…

upper-fort-garry.s: Upper Fort Garry was a Hudson's Bay Company post built in the 1830s at the junction of the Red and Assiniboine rivers, in present-day Winnipeg. It was the administrative centre of the Red River Colony, and in November 1869 Louis Riel's Métis seized it and made it the seat of…

union-for-national-progress.s: The Union for National Progress (UPRONA) is a Burundian political party founded in the late 1950s and led to victory in the 1961 elections by Prince Louis Rwagasore. After independence it became the single ruling party, dominated by the Tutsi military under Michel Micombero,…

upper-valais.s: The Upper Valais is the German-speaking eastern part of the canton of Valais in Switzerland, along the upper Rhône from the Rhône Glacier to around Leuk. Its communes, the Zenden, gradually took power from the prince-bishops of Sion and ruled the French-speaking Lower Valais…

uhtua.s: Uhtua, now called Kalevala, is a village in the north of the Republic of Karelia in Russia, on Lake Middle Kuyto. Many of the folk poems that Elias Lönnrot used for the Kalevala were collected in the surrounding White Sea Karelia region.

unilateral-declaration-of-independence-r.s: The Unilateral Declaration of Independence was issued on 11 November 1965 by Ian Smith's Rhodesian Front government of Southern Rhodesia, which refused Britain's demand for progress to majority rule. Britain and the United Nations declared it illegal and imposed sanctions, and…

uppland.s: Uppland is a historical province of eastern Sweden, north of Stockholm, around Lake Mälaren and Uppsala. It was the heartland of the Svear, the people from whom Sweden takes its name, and Old Uppsala was the seat of early kings and a pagan cult centre.

upplands-norway.s: The Upplands (Opplandene) were the inland districts of eastern Norway, including Hadeland, Ringerike, Hedmark, Toten and Gudbrandsdal. In the Viking age they were divided among petty kings and shared the Eidsivating law assembly.

upper-peru.s: Upper Peru was the name of the highland territory of the Royal Audiencia of Charcas in the Spanish empire, corresponding roughly to modern Bolivia. Rich in silver from Potosí, it belonged to the Viceroyalty of Peru until 1776 and then to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata.

university-of-san-francisco-xavier.s: The University of San Francisco Xavier in Sucre, Bolivia, was founded by the Jesuits in 1624 and is one of the oldest universities in the Americas. In the late colonial period its law faculty and academy educated many leaders of the independence movements of Upper Peru and the…

urogs.s: The Urogs were a people of the western Eurasian steppe recorded by the Byzantine historian Priscus. In 463 they, with the Saragurs and Onogurs, sent envoys to Constantinople after being driven west by the Sabirs.

union-island.s: Union Island is one of the southern Grenadines, part of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, with its main village at Clifton. In December 1979, weeks after independence, a brief armed uprising there was put down with help from Barbados.

unity-labour-party.s: The Unity Labour Party is a centre-left political party in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, formed in 1994 by the merger of the Saint Vincent Labour Party and the Movement for National Unity. Led by Ralph Gonsalves, it won the election of 2001 and governed for five successive…

usrushana.s: Usrushana was a historical region of Central Asia between Samarkand and Khujand, south of the Syr Darya, in modern northern Tajikistan. Ruled by local princes with the title afshin, it was conquered by the Abbasids in the early 9th century.

uttaradit.s: Uttaradit is a town in northern Thailand on the Nan river and the capital of Uttaradit Province. The area was an important river port linking northern Thailand with the central plains.

ulamburiash.s: Ulamburiash was a Kassite prince, brother of the Babylonian king Kashtiliash III, who around 1460 BCE conquered the Sealand Dynasty of southern Mesopotamia after its king Ea-gamil fled to Elam. The conquest brought all of Babylonia, which the Kassites called Karduniash, under…

uysyn.s: The Uysyn are a tribe of the Senior Jüz of the Kazakhs, living in southern and south-eastern Kazakhstan. They were nomadic herders whose pastures lay near the cities of Tashkent and Turkistan.

usambara-mountains.s: The Usambara Mountains are a range in north-eastern Tanzania, part of the ancient Eastern Arc Mountains. Their forests are famous for their rich wildlife and plants, including the wild African violet.

ubar-tutu.s: Ubar-Tutu is the last king before the flood in the Sumerian King List, said to have ruled at Shuruppak for thousands of years. Some versions of the flood tradition make him the father of the flood hero Ziusudra, called Utnapishtim in the Epic of Gilgamesh.

urnes-stave-church.s: Urnes Stave Church is a wooden church on the Lustrafjord, a branch of the Sognefjord in western Norway, built around 1130 and among the oldest surviving stave churches. It reuses carved timbers from an earlier church whose interlaced animal ornament gave its name to the Urnes…

umar-marvi.s: Umar Marvi is a Sindhi folk tale about Marvi, a village girl from the Thar desert who was abducted by Umar, a Soomra king of Umarkot, but refused his wealth and stayed faithful to her people and her betrothed until she was released. Retold by the poet Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai…

university-of-dublin.s: The University of Dublin is Ireland's oldest university, founded in 1592 by a charter of Elizabeth I, with Trinity College Dublin as its only college. For centuries a Protestant institution of the Anglo-Irish establishment, it educated figures such as Jonathan Swift and Edmund…

union-of-arras.s: The Union of Arras was an agreement of 6 January 1579 by which the Catholic southern provinces of Artois and Hainaut, with the towns of Walloon Flanders, declared their loyalty to Philip II of Spain during the Dutch Revolt. It led to a formal reconciliation with the king in…

u-nu.s: U Nu (1907–1995) was a Burmese nationalist and statesman who became the first prime minister of independent Burma in 1948. A leader of the Thakin movement and foreign minister in Ba Maw's wartime government, he succeeded the murdered Aung San as head of the Anti-Fascist…

united-nations-transitional-authority-in.s: The United Nations Transitional Authority in Cambodia was a peacekeeping and administrative mission set up under the Paris Peace Agreements, operating from March 1992 to September 1993 under Yasushi Akashi. With some 22,000 military and civilian personnel it was then the…

utah.s: Utah is a state in the western United States, with its capital at Salt Lake City. Settled from 1847 by members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints led by Brigham Young, it was organised as Utah Territory in 1850 after the Mormons' proposed State of Deseret was…

utah-territory.s: Utah Territory was an organised territory of the United States created by the Compromise of 1850 from part of the lands taken from Mexico, replacing the Mormon-proposed State of Deseret. Brigham Young was its first governor until federal troops arrived in the Utah War of…

university-of-utah.s: The University of Utah is a public research university in Salt Lake City. It was founded in 1850 by the General Assembly of the State of Deseret as the University of Deseret, closed for lack of funds after two years and reopened in 1867.

umhlanga.s: Umhlanga, the reed dance, is an annual ceremony of the Swazi Kingdom (Eswatini), held in late August or early September. Tens of thousands of unmarried girls and young women cut tall reeds and bring them to the queen mother's royal village at Ludzidzini to repair its…

unye.s: Ünye is a port town on the Black Sea coast of northern Turkey, in Ordu province. Known to the Greeks as Oinaion, it was part of the Empire of Trebizond before passing in the 14th century to Turkmen beyliks of the Pontic hinterland such as the Taceddinids, and it came under…

ucles.s: Uclés is a village in the province of Cuenca, Spain. In the 11th century it was a stronghold of the Banu Dhi al-Nun, later lords of Toledo, and in 1108 the Almoravids defeated a Castilian army there, killing Sancho, the only son of Alfonso VI.

united-tajik-opposition.s: The United Tajik Opposition was the coalition of Islamist and democratic groups that fought the government of Emomali Rahmon in the Tajik civil war of 1992–1997. Led by Sayid Abdulloh Nuri, with the Islamic Renaissance Party at its core, it operated largely from Afghanistan.

urhi-teshub.s: Urhi-Teshub, who reigned as Mursili III, was king of the Hittites for several years in the early 13th century BCE, son of Muwatalli II. He moved the capital back from Tarhuntassa to Hattusa but was overthrown by his uncle Hattusili III after a civil war.

ubii.s: The Ubii were a Germanic people who lived on the right bank of the Rhine and became allies of Rome under Julius Caesar. Under Augustus's general Agrippa they were resettled on the left bank, where their chief settlement, the Oppidum Ubiorum, became the Roman colony of Colonia…

ulfilas.s: Ulfilas, or Wulfila, was a Gothic bishop of Cappadocian descent who converted many Goths to Arian Christianity. Consecrated around 341, he worked among the Thervingi north of the Danube and, after persecution by Athanaric, led his followers into Roman Moesia.

united-state-of-greater-rajasthan.s: The United State of Greater Rajasthan was a union of former princely states formed on 30 March 1949 by merging the United State of Rajasthan with Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner and Jaisalmer. Jaipur became its capital, Man Singh II of Jaipur its Rajpramukh and the Maharana of…

udai-singh-ii.s: Udai Singh II was Maharana of Mewar until his death in 1572 and the founder of the city of Udaipur in 1559. A son of Rana Sanga, he escaped as a child from the usurper Banvir, who had killed his brother Vikramaditya, and later won back the throne.

uesugi-norimasa.s: Uesugi Norimasa was the Kantō kanrei, the shogun's deputy for eastern Japan, from the Yamanouchi branch of the Uesugi family. Defeated by the Later Hōjō clan, notably at the Battle of Kawagoe in 1546, he lost his base in Kōzuke and fled to Echigo, to his family's former deputy…

ui-chonaill-gabra.s: The Uí Chonaill Gabra were a branch of the Uí Fidgenti of early medieval Munster, holding territory in western County Limerick, where the barony of Connello preserves their name. Their kings, later known by the surname Ó Coileáin (Collins), lost their lands to Anglo-Norman…

ukrainisation.s: Ukrainisation was the Soviet policy of the 1920s and early 1930s that promoted the Ukrainian language and ethnic Ukrainians in the schools, press, culture and administration of the Ukrainian SSR. It was the Ukrainian form of korenizatsiia, the Bolshevik policy of rooting…

umma.s: Umma was a Sumerian city in southern Mesopotamia, at the site of Tell Jokha in Dhi Qar province, Iraq, north-west of Lagash. Its patron god was Shara.

unitarian-party.s: The Unitarian Party was a political faction in Argentina in the decades after independence that favoured a centralised state led from Buenos Aires, liberal reforms and European-style institutions. Its leaders included Bernardino Rivadavia and General José María Paz.

united-arab-states.s: The United Arab States was a loose confederation formed in March 1958 between the United Arab Republic of Egypt and Syria and the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen under Imam Ahmad. It had no real common institutions, and each member kept its own government.

united-states-bill-of-rights.s: The United States Bill of Rights is the first ten amendments to the United States Constitution, proposed by Congress in 1789 and ratified in 1791. Drafted largely by James Madison to answer Anti-Federalist fears of a strong central government, it guarantees freedom of…

ulleungdo.s: Ulleungdo is a volcanic island in the Sea of Japan (East Sea), about 120 kilometres off the east coast of Korea. It was the centre of the small state of Usan, which the Silla general Isabu subdued in 512 according to the Samguk sagi.

uwajima.s: Uwajima is a port city in Ehime Prefecture on the western coast of Shikoku, Japan, facing the Bungo Channel. Its castle, rebuilt by the Date family in the 1660s, is one of the few in Japan with an original keep.

uttararamacharita.s: The Uttararamacharita ('The Later Story of Rama') is a Sanskrit drama in seven acts by Bhavabhuti, written in the 8th century. It treats Rama's banishment of Sita and their final reunion with their sons, changing the tragic ending of the Ramayana into a reconciliation.

ulaca.s: Ulaca is a large Iron Age hillfort near Solosancho in the province of Ávila, Spain, and one of the main oppida of the Vettones, enclosing more than 60 hectares within its walls. It is known for a rock-cut altar with steps, usually interpreted as a place of sacrifice, and a…

undavalli-caves.s: The Undavalli Caves are rock-cut Hindu cave temples carved into a sandstone hill on the south bank of the Krishna near Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, India. Generally attributed to the period of the Vishnukundina kings in the 5th to 7th centuries, the largest is a four-storeyed…

union-of-three-nations.s: The Union of Three Nations (Unio Trium Nationum) was a pact of mutual aid formed in 1437 at Kápolna by the Hungarian nobility, the Saxons and the Székelys of Transylvania against the peasant revolt of Budai Nagy Antal, and renewed at Torda in 1438. It became the basis of…

ulithi.s: Ulithi is an atoll in the western Caroline Islands, part of Yap State in the Federated States of Micronesia, with one of the largest lagoons in the world. Through the sawei exchange system its chiefs owed tribute to the Gagil district of Yap and received protection in return.

uyghur-muqam.s: The Uyghur Muqam is the classical music tradition of the Uyghurs of Xinjiang, a set of large suites combining songs, dances, poetry and instrumental music. Tradition credits the compilation of the Twelve Muqam to Amannisa Khan at the court of the Yarkent Khanate in the 16th…

usumacinta-river.s: The Usumacinta River rises in the highlands of Guatemala and flows north-west to the Gulf of Mexico, for much of its course forming the border between Mexico and Guatemala. In the Classic period it was a major trade route of the Maya world, lined by rival kingdoms such as…

urumqi.s: Urumqi is the capital of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China, lying in an oasis on the northern side of the Tian Shan. A small settlement in earlier centuries, it grew after the Qing conquest of Dzungaria in the 1750s as a garrison town called Dihua, and became the…

uele-river.s: The Uele River flows west across the north of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and joins the Mbomu to form the Ubangi, a tributary of the Congo. Its basin was home to the Mangbetu and Zande kingdoms, famous for their court arts, and was reached by the German explorer Georg…

ulundi.s: Ulundi is a town in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, on the plain of the White Mfolozi river. King Cetshwayo built his royal homestead, oNdini, there in the 1870s, and the British burned it after defeating the Zulu army nearby in July 1879.

umayyad-invasion-of-gaul.s: The Umayyad invasion of Gaul was the series of campaigns launched from al-Andalus into Frankish territory after 719, when Narbonne was taken. Raids reached deep into Aquitaine and Burgundy until Charles Martel defeated Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi between Tours and Poitiers in 732.

uprising-of-asen-and-peter.s: The Uprising of Asen and Peter was the revolt of the Bulgarians and Vlachs of the Balkan Mountains against Byzantine rule, begun in 1185 by the brothers Theodore-Peter and Ivan Asen. Sparked by heavy taxation, it defeated several Byzantine expeditions and by 1187 had…

unesco.s: UNESCO, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, is a specialised agency of the United Nations founded in 1945 and based in Paris. It promotes international cooperation in education, science, culture and communication.
